==English== {{wp}} ===Etymology 1=== {{ety|en|id=noun|:inh|enm:spanne|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|spanne}}, from {{inh|en|ang|spann}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*spannō|t=span, handbreadth}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)pend-|t=to stretch}}.{{R:AHD|span}} Cognate with {{cog|nl|span}}, {{m|nl|spanne}}, {{cog|de|Spanne}}. {{senseno|en|two animals|cap=1}} is probably from {{cog|ang|ġespan}}, {{m|ang|ġespann|t=a joining; a fastening together; clasp; yoke}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|-}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|gespan}} and {{cog|de|Gespann}}. ====Pronunciation==== * {{IPA|en|/spæn/|a=RP,GA}} * {{IPA|en|/span/|a=SSB,Northern England,Scotland,Wales}} * {{IPA|en|/spæːn/|a=AU}} * {{IPA|en|/spɛn/|a=NZ}} * {{audio|en|en-us-span.ogg|a=US}} * {{rhymes|en|æn|s=1}} * {{hyph|en|span}} ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # {{sid|en|width}} The [[full]] [[width]] of an [[open]] [[hand]], from the [[end]] of the [[thumb]] to the [[end]] of the [[little finger]], [[use]]d as an [[informal]] [[unit of measure|unit]] of [[length]]. # {{sid|en|units}} Any of various [[traditional]] units of [[length]] approximating this [[distance]]; especially: #* {{quote-book|en|year=2003|origyear=1605|author=w:Miguel de Cervantes|tlr=w:Edith Grossman|original=Don Quixote|origlang=es|title=w:Don Quixote|page=109 |passage=The truth is that the charm of her body made up for her other faults: she measured less than 7 '''spans''' from her feet to the top of her head, and her back, which weighed somewhat heavily on her, forced her to look down at the ground more than she would have wished. |footer=The translation contains a footnote: "A '''span''' is approximately eight inches".}} ## {{sid|en|handspan}} The [[English]] [[handspan]], equivalent to 9 inches or 22.86 cm. # {{sid|en|spacetime}} {{lb|en|by extension}} A small space or a brief [[moment]] of time. #: {{co|en|attention '''span'''}} #: {{ux|en|He has a short attention '''span''' and gets bored within minutes.}} #* {{RQ:Haggard She|passage="Why in ten thousand years scarce will the rain and storms lessen a mountain top by a '''span''' in thickness?"}} #* {{RQ:Pope Universal Prayer|stanza=VI|page=5|passage=Yet not to Earth's contracted '''Span''',
Thy Goodneſs let me bound; {{...}}}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1699|author=w:George Farquhar|title=w:The Constant Couple |passage=Life's but a '''span'''; I'll every inch enjoy.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2007|author=John Zerzan|title=Silence |passage=The unsilent present is a time of evaporating attention '''spans''',}} # {{sid|en|subsequence}} A segment or portion of space or time; a [[subsequence]]. #* {{quote-book|en|year=2004|author=Robert Harris; Robert Warner|title=The Definitive Guide to SWT and JFace|page=759 |passage=For example, in OpenOffice.org or Microsoft Word, each '''span''' of text can have a style that defines key characteristics about the text: • What font it uses • Whether it's normal, bolded, italicized, {{...}}}} ## {{sid|en|computing}} {{lb|en|computing}} The time required to execute a [[parallel]] algorithm on an infinite number of processors. # {{sid|en|architec1}} {{lb|en|architecture|construction}} The spread or extent of an [[arch]] or between its [[abutment]]s, or of a beam, [[girder]], [[truss]], [[roof]], [[bridge]], or the like, between [[support]]s. # {{sid|en|architec2}} {{lb|en|architecture|construction}} The length of a [[cable]], [[wire]], [[rope]], [[chain]] between two consecutive [[support]]s. # {{sid|en|nautical}} {{lb|en|nautical}} A rope having its ends made fast so that a purchase can be hooked to the [[bight]]; also, a rope made fast in the center so that both ends can be used. # {{sid|en|two animals}} {{lb|en|US|Canada|collective}} A pair of [[horse]]s or other animals driven or sold together; usually, such a pair of [[horse]]s usually being similar in color, form, and action. # {{sid|en|Q209812}} {{lb|en|linear algebra}} {{ellipsis of|en|linear span}}: a [[linear subspace]] generated by all [[linear combination]]s of a given [[subset]] of [[vector]]s of a given [[vector space]]. # {{sid|en|wingspan}} {{clipping of|en|wingspan}}. =====Derived terms===== {{col|en |affine ====See also==== * {{l|en|chord}} ===Etymology 2=== From {{inh|en|enm|spannen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|spannan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*spannaną|t=to stretch, span}}. Cognate with {{cog|de|spannen}}, {{cog|nl|spannen}}. ====Pronunciation==== * {{IPA|en|/spæn/|a=RP,GenAm}} * {{IPA|en|/spæːn/|a=AU}} * {{rhymes|en|æn|s=1}} ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} {{tlb|en|transitive}} # {{sid|en|extend across}} To extend across (a gap or space between two sides). #: {{ux|en|The suspension bridge '''spanned''' the canyon.}} #* {{RQ:Prescott Philip 2|passage=The rivers were '''spanned''' by arches of solid masonry.}} # {{sid|en|extend over}} To cover or extend over (an area or distance). #: {{ux|en|The parking lot '''spans''' three acres.}} #: {{ux|en|The forest '''spans''' the entire valley.}} # {{sid|en|extend through}} To extend through (a period of time). #: {{ux|en|The novel '''spans''' three centuries.}} #: {{ux|en|His career '''spanned''' five decades.}} # {{sid|en|measure}} To measure by the span of the hand with the fingers extended, or with the fingers encompassing the object. #: {{ux|en|to '''span''' a space or distance; to '''span''' a cylinder}} #* {{RQ:KJV|Isaiah|48|13|page=802|column=2|text=Mine hand alſo hath laid the foundation of the earth, and my right hand hath '''ſpanned''' the heauens: ''when'' I call vnto them, they ſtand vp together.}} # {{sid|en|linalg}} {{lb|en|linear algebra}} To generate a [[linear span]]. # {{sid|en|be matched}} {{lb|en|intransitive|US|dated|of horses}} To be matched. # {{sid|en|fetter}} {{lb|en|of a horse}} To [[fetter]]; to [[hobble]]. #* {{quote-journal|en|year=1972|journal=Mountain|issue=20-24|page=22 |passage=We '''spanned''' the dogs high up a corrie to the south of the ridge {{...}}}} =====Translations===== {{trans-top-see|to extend through the distance between or across|cover|cross}} * Azerbaijani: * Bulgarian: * Finnish: * French: * German: * Hungarian: * Italian: * Japanese: * Lithuanian: * Māori: * Mari: * Portuguese: * Russian: {{t+|ru|раскидываться}}, {{t+|ru|растягиваться}} * Slovak: * Spanish: * Swedish: * Tamil: * Ukrainian: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top-see|to cover or extend over an area or distance|cover}} * Spanish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top-see|to extend through a period of time|comprise}} * Bulgarian: * Finnish: * French: * Hungarian: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Spanish: * Swedish: * Ukrainian: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|to measure by the span of the hand}} * Turkish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|linear algebra: to generate a linear span}} * German: * Swedish: {{trans-bottom}} ===Etymology 3=== From {{inh|en|enm|span}}, from {{inh|en|ang|spann}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*spann}}, first and third person singular preterit indicative of {{der|en|gem-pro|*spinnaną|t=to spin}}. ====Pronunciation==== * {{IPA|en|/spæn/|a=RP,AusE,GenAm}} * {{rhymes|en|æn|s=1}} ====Verb==== {{head|en|verb form}} # {{lb|en|dated|now|uncommon}} {{infl of|en|spin||spast}} #* {{RQ:Jack Straw|I|18|But when ''Adam'' delued, and ''Eue'' '''ſpan''',
